# Command line reference

Every command, its flags, and what it does. Every command accepts the global flags `--json`, `--debug`, and `--help`. Exit codes are 0 (done), 1 (could not complete), 2 (the command line was wrong); see [exit-codes.md](exit-codes.md).

## Setup

### `construct init`

set this project up: files, one database, a drafted profile, the operational skill in your host

| Flag | Takes a value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--name` | yes | the project’s name (default: the directory or package name) |
| `--purpose` | yes | what the project is for, in a sentence |
| `--scale` | yes | what this is to you: solo \| side_project \| team \| multi_team \| organization |
| `--outcome` | yes | the result that matters most right now |
| `--constraint` | yes, repeatable | something Construct must be careful not to change or violate |
| `--client` | yes | the host you use: plants its skill and wires its MCP config (claude-code \| cursor \| vscode \| opencode, bob, codex) |
| `--no-wire` | no | do not write the host’s MCP configuration |
| `--skills-dir` | yes | plant the operational skill into this directory instead of a host’s |
| `--dry-run` | no | say what would happen and write nothing |

Reads only: no.

### `construct project refresh`

re-read the project’s own files and propose updates; confirms nothing

Reads only: no.

### `construct status`

## Configure

### `construct config list`

Reads only: yes.

### `construct config get <key>`

Reads only: yes.

Reads only: yes.

### `construct config path`

Reads only: yes.

### `construct config validate`

check the user and project configuration files

Reads only: yes.

### `construct config set <key> <value>`

| Flag | Takes a value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--scope` | yes | which file to write: project or user (default: whichever may hold the key) |

Reads only: no.

### `construct config unset <key>`

remove one setting from the project or user file

| Flag | Takes a value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--scope` | yes | which file to write: project or user (default: whichever may hold the key) |

Reads only: no.

## Sources

### `construct source list`

every active source with reachability and freshness

Reads only: yes.

### `construct source show <id>`

one source: purpose, authority, freshness, last read

Reads only: yes.

### `construct source add <id>`

declare a source (committed) or add one only this checkout knows (--local)

| Flag | Takes a value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--kind` | yes | one of directory \| git \| github \| jira \| docs \| hris \| other |
| `--purpose` | yes | what this source is for, in a sentence |
| `--locator` | yes | where it is: a path, PROJ, owner/repo, provider:container:id |
| `--authority` | yes | overall trust: authoritative \| informative \| untrusted (default informative) |
| `--authoritative-for` | yes, repeatable | a claim type this source settles |
| `--not-authoritative-for` | yes, repeatable | a claim type this source must not settle |
| `--sensitivity` | yes | public \| internal \| confidential \| restricted (default internal) |
| `--freshness-hours` | yes | how old a read may be before it is stale |
| `--write` | no | this source may be written to (still gated per action) |
| `--local` | no | keep it out of the committed file; the locator may be sensitive |

Reads only: no.

### `construct source retire <id>`

retire a source; its history stays

Reads only: no.

### `construct source refresh <id>`

read a source now and record what changed

Reads only: no.

### `construct source relate <from-id> <relation> <to-id>`

record how two sources stand to each other: governs | depends_on | feeds | supersedes | contradicts

Reads only: no.

## Skills

### `construct skill list`

the skills this install ships, with versions

Reads only: yes.

### `construct skill show <name>`

one skill’s description, version, and files

Reads only: yes.

### `construct skill install <name>`

plant a shipped skill into a host’s skills directory, byte for byte

| Flag | Takes a value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--dir` | yes | the skills directory to use instead of the detected host’s |
| `--client` | yes | the host whose skills directory to use: claude \| bob \| opencode \| cursor \| codex |
| `--force` | no | overwrite a copy that differs |

Reads only: no.

### `construct skill verify`

compare installed skills with the shipped ones

| Flag | Takes a value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--dir` | yes | the skills directory to use instead of the detected host’s |
| `--client` | yes | the host whose skills directory to use: claude \| bob \| opencode \| cursor \| codex |

Reads only: yes.

### `construct skill update`

bring the project’s registry lock up to the skills and workflows present; project-authored changes are locked only when named

| Flag | Takes a value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--confirm` | yes, repeatable | a project-authored bundle id whose change may be locked (repeatable) |
| `--dry-run` | no | report what would change |

Reads only: no.

### `construct skill remove <name>`

remove an installed skill (needs --confirm)

| Flag | Takes a value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--dir` | yes | the skills directory to use instead of the detected host’s |
| `--client` | yes | the host whose skills directory to use: claude \| bob \| opencode \| cursor \| codex |
| `--confirm` | no | actually remove it |

Reads only: no.

## Workflows

### `construct workflow list`

the workflows this project can run, with versions and what starts them

Reads only: yes.

### `construct workflow show <id>`

one workflow: purpose, steps, tiers, inputs, policies

Reads only: yes.

### `construct workflow resolve <id>`

can this workflow run here now, and what would stop it

| Flag | Takes a value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--input` | yes, repeatable | a key=value input (repeatable) |

Reads only: yes.

### `construct workflow run <id>`

start a run of a workflow from the command line (the host does the steps)

| Flag | Takes a value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--input` | yes, repeatable | a key=value input (repeatable) |
| `--dry-run` | no | resolve and report; start nothing |

Reads only: no.

### `construct workflow validate`

check every skill and workflow bundle this project can see

Reads only: yes.

### `construct workflow schedule <id>`

define a standing trigger for a workflow, fired by cron or CI

| Flag | Takes a value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--cron` | yes | five-field cron expression |
| `--timezone` | yes | IANA timezone for the expression (default UTC) |
| `--event` | yes | an event name instead of a schedule |
| `--adapter` | yes | who fires it: manual \| cron \| ci \| host (default cron) |
| `--overlap` | yes | skip \| queue \| replace when a run is still active (default skip) |
| `--max-tier` | yes | the highest tier a firing may act at: observe \| draft \| project_write \| external_write \| destructive |
| `--input` | yes, repeatable | a key=value input (repeatable) |
| `--trigger-id` | yes | a stable id for the trigger |

Reads only: no.

### `construct workflow triggers`

the standing triggers defined here, with next due and last fired

Reads only: yes.

### `construct workflow enable <trigger-id>`

enable a standing trigger

Reads only: no.

### `construct workflow disable <trigger-id>`

disable a standing trigger; nothing fires until enabled

Reads only: no.

### `construct workflow fire <trigger-id>`

fire a trigger now, as an external clock would

| Flag | Takes a value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--key` | yes | the clock’s key for this tick (same key, same run) |
| `--dry-run` | no | preflight only |

Reads only: no.

### `construct workflow recipe <trigger-id>`

print the cron line or CI job that fires a trigger

| Flag | Takes a value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--clock` | yes | cron or github-actions (default cron) |

Reads only: yes.

## Host

### `construct serve`

speak MCP over stdio for the host that launched it, bound to this project

| Flag | Takes a value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--client` | yes | which host is on the other end: claude-code \| cursor \| vscode \| opencode \| codex \| bob \| unknown |
| `--project` | yes | the project root to bind (default: found from the working directory) |
| `--headless` | no | serve the runner surface instead of the person’s session |
| `--executor` | yes | the runner’s id, with --headless |
| `--describe` | no | print the surface this would serve and exit |

Reads only: no.

## Recover

### `construct reset`

name the Construct-owned files that would be removed; with --confirm, remove exactly them and start clean

| Flag | Takes a value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--confirm` | no | remove the named targets |
| `--include-project-files` | no | also remove the committed .construct files, not only runtime state |
| `--keep-state` | no | do not recreate state after removing |

Reads only: no.

## Global flags

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | print the record as one line of JSON instead of prose |
| `--debug` | include stack traces in failures |
| `--help` | show this command’s help |
